title: Ultrasound-guided vascular access: peripheral, central and arterial
summary: Learn to place peripheral lines, check a central line guidewire and place a radial arterial line with ultrasound. Centre the vein, use a light hand, stop at the near wall, rescue a catheter that will not thread and see the wire before you dilate.
author: Dr Firas Abou-Auda, Consultant in Emergency Medicine and Course Director, Wavelength
conflicts: Dr Firas Abou-Auda is Course Director of Wavelength, which runs paid ultrasound courses.
audience: Emergency and acute care doctors, advanced clinical practitioners, nurses and others who place, or are training to place, vascular access with ultrasound under their trust's governance.
outcomes: Choose when ultrasound helps most for peripheral cannulation and prepare the limb and the image
Tell a vein from an artery with compression, and use colour and spectral Doppler with their limits
Avoid a posterior wall puncture and rescue a catheter that will not thread, using short and long axis
Confirm that a guidewire lies inside the internal jugular vein, in two views, before you dilate
Place a radial arterial line by choosing a straight segment and rescuing in long axis
references: Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. Ultrasound guidance for peripheral intravenous cannulation in adults. 2022; CD013434.
